title: “After this lived Job an hundred and forty years” — the Greek has a hundred and seventy, and a total of two hundred and forty
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, says Job lived a hundred and forty years after his trial and gives no total. Brenton’s Greek says a hundred and seventy years after it, and adds that all the years he lived were two hundred and forty.
text: KJV Job 42:16: “After this lived Job an hundred and forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons' sons, even four generations.” Hebrew (WLC) 42:16: וַיְחִ֤י אִיֹּוב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה [and Job lived after this a hundred and forty years]. reasoning: The figure for the years after the trial is 140 in the KJV and 170 in the Greek. The Greek also states a whole lifetime, 240 years; the KJV verse states none.

title: “So Job died, being old and full of days” — the Greek goes on: he will rise again, and he was Jobab, a king of Edom
summary: The KJV, with the Hebrew, ends the book at Job’s death. Brenton’s Greek prints five more paragraphs: that it is written he will rise again with those the Lord raises; that he lived on the borders of Idumea and Arabia and was first called Jobab; his parents, wife and son; a list of kings of Edom with him as the second; and the three friends as kings.
text: KJV Job 42:17, the last verse of the book: “So Job died, being old and full of days.” Hebrew (WLC) 42:17, the last verse of the book in that edition: וַיָּ֣מָת אִיֹּ֔וב זָקֵ֖ן וּשְׂבַ֥ע יָמִֽים. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 42:17: Καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν Ἰὼβ πρεσβύτερος, καὶ πλήρης ἡμερῶν· The page then prints five passages under the labels 17a to 17e. 17a: γέγραπται δὲ, αὐτὸν πάλιν ἀναστήσεσθαι μεθʼ ὧν ὁ Κύριος ἀνίστησιν. [and it is written that he will rise again with those whom the Lord raises up.] 17b: Οὗτος ἑρμηνεύεται ἐκ τῆς Συριακῆς βίβλου, ἐν μὲν γῇ κατοικῶν τῇ Αὐσίτιδι, ἐπὶ τοῖς ὁρίοις τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ Ἀραβίας· προϋπῆρχε δὲ αὐτῷ ὄνομα Ἰωβάβ· [This man is interpreted out of the Syriac book as dwelling in the land of Ausis, on the borders of Idumea and Arabia; and his name before was Jobab;] 17c: λαβὼν δὲ γυναῖκα Ἀράβισσαν, γεννᾷ υἱὸν, ᾧ ὄνομα Ἐννών· ἦν δὲ αὐτὸς πατρὸς μὲν Ζαρὲ ἐκ τῶν Ἡσαῦ υἱῶν υἱὸς, μητρὸς δὲ Βοσόῤῥας, ὥστε εἶναι αὐτὸν πέμπτον ἀπὸ Ἁβραάμ· [and having taken an Arabian wife, he begets a son whose name is Ennon; and he himself was the son of his father Zare, of the sons of Esau, and of his mother Bosorrha, so that he was the fifth from Abraam;] 17d: καὶ οὗτοι οἱ βασιλεῖς οἱ βασιλεύσαντες ἐν Ἐδὼμ, ἧς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦρξε χώρας· πρῶτος Βαλὰκ ὁ τοῦ Βεὼρ, καὶ ὄνομα τῇ πόλει αὐτοῦ Δενναβά· μετὰ δὲ Βαλὰκ, Ἰωβὰβ ὁ καλούμενος Ἰώβ· μετὰ δὲ τοῦτον, Ἀσὼμ ὁ ὑπάρχων ἡγεμὼν ἐκ τῆς Θαιμανίτιδος χώρας· μετὰ δὲ τοῦτον, Ἀδὰδ υἱὸς Βαρὰδ, ὁ ἐκκόψας Μαδιὰμ ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ Μωὰβ, καὶ ὄνομα τῇ πόλει αὐτοῦ Γεθαίμ· [and these are the kings who reigned in Edom, which country he also governed: first Balak the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dennaba; and after Balak, Jobab who is called Job; and after him Asom, who was governor from the country of Thaeman; and after him Adad son of Barad, who cut off Madiam in the plain of Moab, and the name of his city was Gethaim;] 17e: οἱ δὲ ἐλθόντες πρὸς αὐτὸν φίλοι, Ἐλιφὰς τῶν Ἡσαῦ υἱῶν Θαιμανῶν βασιλεὺς, Βαλδὰδ ὁ Σαυχαίων τύραννος, Σωφὰρ ὁ Μιναίων βασιλεύς. [and the friends who came to him: Eliphas, of the sons of Esau, king of the Thaemans; Baldad, sovereign of the Sauchaeans; Sophar, king of the Minaeans.] For comparison, the KJV’s list of kings of Edom. Genesis 36:32: “And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.” Genesis 36:33: “And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.” Genesis 36:34: “And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.” Genesis 36:35: “And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.” KJV Job 2:11 on the friends: “Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite” Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/18/42/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOB42.htm.
reasoning: The KJV and the Hebrew edition end the book with Job’s death. In the KJV verses compared (Job 1:1–5, 2:11 and 42:7–17) nothing says that Job had another name, that he governed a country, or who his parents were, and no sentence about his rising again follows his death. The Greek’s list of kings runs in the order of Genesis 36:32–35 and puts Job in the place where the KJV of Genesis has “Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah”. The Greek ending names as its source “the Syriac book” and, for the rising again, says only “it is written”.
scope: G applies at 42:17, the verse after which the added passages are printed. The KJV of Job, in the verses compared (1:1–5, 2:11, 42:7–17), neither states nor denies what the ending adds, so this is a longer text and not a conflict. The KJV of Genesis names a Jobab among the kings of Edom but does not call him Job; whether the two are one man is the Greek ending’s statement, not the KJV’s. In Genesis 36:33 “Bozrah” is joined to Jobab as “of Bozrah”; the Greek ending names Bosorrha as his mother. Other names in the Greek list differ in form from the KJV’s of Genesis (Balak and Bela, Asom and Husham, Gethaim and Avith); this record does not say they are different men or the same. Job’s own speeches about death and rising (for example Job 14 and 19) were not compared here. The ending does not say which book “the Syriac book” is, or where the rising again “is written”.
